issues.legal_issue: A statutory board may delegate to its commissioner the authority to appoint a temporary mutawalli, and rules assigning appointments to the board do not prevent the commissioner from acting once that delegation has been made.
material_facts: While two brothers disputed who was entitled to succeed as mutawalli, the commissioner appointed a third brother as temporary mutawalli.
The board had resolved to authorize the commissioner to exercise and perform its powers and duties under section 40, including the power to appoint a temporary mutawalli.
Government rules provided for the commissioner to report and recommend an appointment and for the board to appoint a mutawalli.
issues.conclusion: The commissioner was competent to make the temporary appointment because the board had delegated that authority; the rules did not displace the delegation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 29 and 40 of the Bengal Wakf Act, 1934, permit the board to authorize the commissioner to exercise and perform the board’s powers and duties, including the power to appoint a temporary mutawalli. The rules must be harmoniously construed with that statutory delegation and cannot restrict the board’s power to delegate; once the relevant authority is delegated, the commissioner acts for the board and the rules cease to apply to that delegated function.

predicates.challenge_to_temporary_appointment: The proceeding challenges a commissioner’s appointment of a temporary officeholder.
predicates.board_delegated_appointment_authority: The board authorized the commissioner to exercise its authority to make the kind of temporary appointment at issue.
predicates.rules_assign_appointment_to_board: Rules provide that the board makes the appointment, rather than the commissioner acting independently.
predicates.commissioner_may_make_temporary_appointm: The commissioner is permitted to make the temporary appointment under the board’s delegated authority.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a temporary appointment, the board has delegated authority to make that appointment, and rules otherwise assign appointments to the board, the commissioner may make the temporary appointment.

issues.legal_issue: An unresolved dispute among rival claimants that obstructs the appointment of a permanent mutawalli is an impediment that permits a temporary appointment.
material_facts: After the first mutawalli died, two sons asserted competing claims to succeed him.
The dispute between the claimants remained unresolved when the commissioner appointed another son as temporary mutawalli.
issues.conclusion: The unresolved dispute obstructed the appointment of a permanent mutawalli and therefore constituted an impediment permitting a temporary appointment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 40 of the Bengal Wakf Act, 1934, allows a temporary mutawalli to be appointed where there is no mutawalli or where an impediment to appointing one appears. An impediment means a hindrance or obstruction, and an unresolved dispute over competing claims can obstruct appointment of a permanent mutawalli.

predicates.challenge_to_temporary_appointment: The proceeding challenges an appointment made temporarily while the permanent officeholder is unsettled.
predicates.rival_claim_dispute_blocks_permanent_app: Competing claims to the permanent office remain unresolved and obstruct the appointment of a permanent officeholder.
predicates.temporary_appointment_is_authorized: A temporary appointment is permitted to address the obstruction to appointing a permanent officeholder.

issues.definition: If a challenge concerns a temporary appointment made while an unresolved rival-claim dispute blocks permanent appointment, the temporary appointment is authorized.

issues.legal_issue: When delegated power and its associated duty are interconnected and cannot be separated, delegation of the power carries the duty with it.
material_facts: The board’s resolution authorized the commissioner to exercise and perform delegated powers and duties, including functions concerning temporary appointments.

The question arose whether delegation of the board’s power could leave the corresponding duty with the board; the court stated that interconnected powers and duties that cannot be separated are delegated together.
issues.conclusion: Where a power and duty are interconnected and cannot be separated, delegation of the power includes delegation of the duty.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that where powers and duties are interconnected and cannot be separated, delegation of the powers carries the duties with it. It referred to Mungoni v. Attorney-General of Northern Rhodesia. The statutory context included section 29 of the Bengal Wakf Act, 1934, which allowed the board to authorize the commissioner to exercise and perform powers and duties conferred or imposed on the board.

predicates.delegation_of_statutory_function: An authority delegates a statutory function to another decision-maker.
predicates.delegated_power_and_duty_interconnected: The delegated power and the associated duty form interconnected parts of the function.
predicates.power_and_duty_cannot_be_separated: The power cannot be delegated while the associated duty is retained, or vice versa.
predicates.delegation_includes_associated_duty: Delegation of the power also delegates the associated duty.

issues.definition: When a statutory function is delegated and its power and duty are interconnected and inseparable, the delegation includes the associated duty.
